Set the VIC raster compare from A, acknowledge its interrupt, and write X and Y to the low and high bytes of the IRQ dispatch vector at $0314/$0315.

Restore Y, X and A from the interrupt stack, then return with RTI. Raster handlers jump here after acknowledging their interrupt.

Select VIC bank 1 and the character display settings, enable multicolour sprites, wait on the raster state, and write sprite positions. It then uses $801A to select a sprite; if its pointer is not $03 and its Y plus $11 is in the range $3C–$F5, it copies twelve bytes from each of two computed sprite addresses to $4033 and $4000, patches the split handler operands and schedules $0922 at Y plus $15. Otherwise it schedules $094E at $F9. The code uses eight-bit arithmetic for these tests.

Acknowledge the interrupt, set the selected sprite's Y and pointer from operands patched by $086D, wait until the raster passes a second Y value, then replace that sprite pointer with the other patched value. Continue to $0942 to schedule the later handler.
Schedule the handler at $094E for raster value $F9, then restore the interrupt registers and return.

Change the display settings, initialize sprite enable, multicolour, coordinates, colours and pointer bytes, call the sound update, and schedule $086D for raster value $0A. It then prepares room sprites before restoring the interrupt registers and returning.
Acknowledge raster interrupt bit 0 through $D019, call the common sound update at $E13A, and jump to the register-restoring interrupt exit at $0867.
Wait for 28 transitions through the high raster bit, then wait for the joystick fire bit at CIA port A to be released and pressed. Tail-call the sound-state clear routine.

Contact state at $9485 and per-player response bytes beginning at $9486. The contact path at $95E8-$95EF clears $9485 and sets $9486,X to 1. The recovery path at $997C/$997E sets $9485 to 1.

State for the animated screen detail. $9488 drives the screen-coordinate selection at $97EC-$9947. The neighboring counters and flags control the player-specific updates that call into this selection.
Three saved three-byte coordinate groups, filled by the paths at $9A9E, $9AE8 and $9B32. The restore paths beginning at $9BA1, $9BDC and $9C17 read the groups back into the active coordinate state.

Mutable position and screen-animation state for the actor paths at $9B9E-$A2CD. The coordinate group $9499-$949B is loaded from the saved triples and changed by the eight-direction motion routines. The remaining bytes hold their counters, flags and saved screen cells; the consuming routines document their separate operations.
Last four bytes of the actor and screen-state group beginning at $9498. The group crosses the listing span limit here; consumers are the same scene-animation paths.

Dispatch the selected first Ghostbuster's weapon: equipment $3D is a toggled proton beam, $3C fires individual slime projectiles. Disable the other player's weapon state when its equipment no longer matches. A new fire press first checks for picking up or putting down Oscar; that interaction suppresses the shot.
Set X=0 and Y=0 and jump to the shared proximity check at $957A.
Set X=1 and Y=2 and jump to the shared proximity check at $957A.

Check same-room proximity to Oscar at $8047/$8048/$8049. On a match, play effect $10, set the indexed pickup-suppression byte $9486,X, change the facing sprite to its carrying counterpart, record the carrier in $947F and set $947E/$8046. The second proton toggle incorrectly tests $9486 rather than its own $9487, so the suppression does not cover that path. Pickup and sprite change were verified in VICE.
Eight facing pointers for an unencumbered Ghostbuster. $9628 maps them to the corresponding Oscar-carrying poses at $9620; $963F reverses the mapping when Oscar is put down.
Eight Oscar-carrying poses, paired by direction with $9618: $AF,$AE,$AD,$A9,$AB,$AA,$A8,$AC. Pickup maps into this table; placing Oscar maps back.
Search the eight bytes at $9618 for the pointer at $FC25,Y. On a match, replace that pointer with the byte at the same index in $9620; return unchanged when no entry matches.
Search the eight bytes at $9620 for the pointer at $FC25,Y. On a match, replace that pointer with the byte at the same index in $9618; return unchanged when no entry matches.
Set X and Y to zero, then jump to the shared placement routine at $96F8.
Set X to 1 and Y to 2, then jump to the shared placement routine at $96F8.

Subtract 1 from each 16-bit address at $99C6/$99C7 and $99CC/$99CD, then subtract 8 from the 16-bit value at $8047/$8048 and return. These values were prepared by the placement routine; the full placement meaning remains open.
Add 1 to each 16-bit address at $99C6/$99C7 and $99CC/$99CD, then add 8 to the 16-bit value at $8047/$8048 and return.
Add 40 to each 16-bit address at $99C6/$99C7 and $99CC/$99CD, then fall through to $96EE, which adds 8 to $8049 and returns.
Add 8 to the byte at $8049 and return. The placement routine calls this twice when its computed row is below 6.

Place carried Oscar in the selected player's room. Convert his lower-body coordinates to a two-row character position, adjusting around scenery codes and the room boundary. Restore the normal facing sprite, clear carrying flag $947E, set dropped flag $9485, and draw the two rows through $9981.

High byte of the self-modified read at $9835; $97E3 sets it from the calculated address. The read byte goes to $9488 and selects calls to $9664 and $9698 for $39–$3B. The value of $8041 selects one of two further groups of comparisons against $9488, with calls to $9664, $9698, $99D2 and $99D9; both paths continue at $9958. The meanings of the tested cell codes remain open.

Set $947F to 4 and use that index to copy values from $CA95 and $CA9A to $CA88 and $CA8E. Set $9486,X to 1, restore the saved Y, preserve X across a call to $963F, clear $947E and set $9485 to 1. Execution then falls into $9981.

Draw Oscar's two-row character image through the patched screen addresses. Copy the four-code templates $99E8/$99EC into working rows, make the two room-0 scenery substitutions, and write either two or four columns as selected by the placement collision checks.
Call the placement-down routine twice and return.
Call the placement-left routine twice and return.
Sixteen bytes used around the $99F0 screen-detail update. They retain the state and saved values adjacent to the routine; the exact independent role of each stored byte is unresolved.
If pickup/drop suppression $9486 is set, clear it and return. Otherwise toggle first-player beam flag $948A. Turning on immediately updates the beam; turning off clears its motion origin when needed.

Update one of the first player's three slime projectiles, enforce the exhausted-energy delay, and detect a newly pressed joystick fire button. Check Oscar pickup or placement before allocating the next projectile. Holding fire does not repeat shots.

Consume pickup/drop suppression if set. Otherwise allocate the first free one of three projectile slots, play effect $0D, consume one weapon-energy row through $C02C, derive its direction and origin from the facing pose, and store the position. The three active flags are $949D-$949F.

Increment the counter at $949C. If it becomes three, reset it to zero and process slot 0 at $9B96; if it becomes one, process slot 1 at $9BD1; otherwise process slot 2 at $9C0C. The routine processes one slot per call.

With X=0, call $9E18 and $9EB4, then call $9F52 with Y=2, then run the direction dispatcher at $9C47 with X=0. The callers first load the selected slot into the shared state at $9498–$949B and copy the updated position back afterward.
Write $03 to $FC2B and return. The three slot handlers jump here when their respective active byte is zero.

If $949D is zero, write $03 to $FC2B and return. Otherwise copy direction $94A0 and position $948F–$9491 into $9498–$949B, select flag index 0 in $94A3, and call $9B79. Copy the updated position back to $948F–$9491.

If $949E is zero, write $03 to $FC2B and return. Otherwise copy direction $94A1 and position $9492–$9494 into $9498–$949B, select flag index 1 in $94A3, and call $9B79. Copy the updated position back to $9492–$9494.

If $949F is zero, write $03 to $FC2B and return. Otherwise copy direction $94A2 and position $9495–$9497 into $9498–$949B, select flag index 2 in $94A3, and call $9B79. Copy the updated position back to $9495–$9497.

Dispatch direction 0-7 to eight slime projectile movement handlers. Each publishes the previous position, selects the corresponding $7C-$83 droplet sprite, then advances its stored position and clears the active flag when it crosses the boundary.

Copy the three state bytes at $9499, $949A and $949B to $FC0B,X, $FC13,X and $FC1B,X, respectively. The caller chooses X. This runs before each directional update, so these destinations receive the previous state.
Clear the selected projectile's active flag: $949D,Y for player 1 or $94B2,Y for player 2. Called when a direction handler crosses the travel boundary.
Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $7C, and subtract 10 from $949B. If the resulting byte is below $28, call $9C94 to clear the selected flag.

Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $7D, and add 10 to the little-endian value at $9499/$949A. If the high byte is nonzero and the low byte is at least $60, clear the selected flag; otherwise subtract 5 from $949B and clear the flag if that result is below $28.
Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $7E, and add 10 to the little-endian value at $9499/$949A. If the high byte is nonzero and the low byte is at least $60, clear the selected flag.

Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $7F, and add 10 to the little-endian value at $9499/$949A. If the high byte is nonzero and the low byte is at least $60, clear the selected flag; otherwise add 5 to $949B and clear the flag if that result is at least $EA.
Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $80, and add 10 to $949B. If the resulting byte is at least $EA, clear the selected flag.

Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $81, and subtract 10 from the little-endian value at $9499/$949A. If the high byte is zero and the low byte is below $10, clear the selected flag; otherwise add 5 to $949B and clear the flag if that result is at least $EA.
Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $82, and subtract 10 from the little-endian value at $9499/$949A. If the high byte is zero and the low byte is below $10, clear the selected flag.

Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $83, and subtract 10 from the little-endian value at $9499/$949A. If the high byte is zero and the low byte is below $10, clear the selected flag; otherwise subtract 5 from $949B and clear the flag if that result is below $28.

Subtract $0C from the two-byte position at $9499/$949A and $32 from $949B. Shift the low-byte results right by three and use the latter to select a word from $8428; combine that word with the shifted first value and the high-byte and $804A,X conditions to patch the address operand at $9E95/$9E96. Read the resulting address at $9E94. If the byte is 1, clear the selected flag in $949D,Y or $94B2,Y according to X. The row table's content and the meaning of value 1 remain open.

In phase 0, test this slime projectile against Janosz in the same room. A hit clears its active flag and calls $A474, which removes two rows from Janosz's strength gauge. Ten uninterrupted hits empty the initial twenty-row gauge. Verified with a positioned projectile in VICE.

Return if $8027 equals 4 for X other than 1, or if $8026 equals 4 for X=1. Also return unless $804A equals $804B. Form half-width horizontal values from $9499/$949A and $FC05,Y/$FC0D,Y; require the first plus 3 to be at least the second and less than the second plus 7. Require $949B to be at least $FC15,Y+6 and less than $FC15,Y+$11, using byte arithmetic. On a match, X=1 clears the selected $94B2 flag and calls $C33D; other values clear the selected $949D flag and call $C35D. The gameplay identity of these compared objects remains open.

Second-player counterpart to $94DC: equipment $3D toggles the proton beam and $3C allocates slime projectiles. Maintains the first player's existing effect, then handles the selected second player's fire edge and Oscar interaction.

Toggle second-player proton beam $948D. This mistakenly checks and clears first-player suppression $9486; pickup/placement for the second player sets $9487 instead. A set $9487 alone therefore does not suppress this toggle. Verified in VICE. Carrying poses separately prevent the beam updater from drawing.

If $FE1D is nonzero, call $FF0D, then call $A1EA. Use $8027 to index $C00C. When the selected byte is nonzero, increment $94DB and, when it reaches $D0, clear it and the selected $C00C byte, then return. Otherwise read CIA 1 port A bit 4, the active-low joystick-port-2 fire line. A release clears the latch $948C. On a new press, set the latch and call $965D if $947E is nonzero and $8027 equals $947F, or call the second interaction check otherwise; then call the interaction-slot initializer. The gating bytes' gameplay meanings remain open, and CIA port configuration can affect the input read.

Allocate one of the second player's three free slime slots, consume one weapon-energy row through $C04C, and save its facing direction and origin. Pickup or placement consumes the triggering press instead of firing.

If $94B3 is clear, initialize the second slot: play effect $0D, call $C04C, set $94B3, call $FEA7, store the resulting direction at $94B6 and position bytes at $94A7–$94A9. Directions 5 or more subtract $10 from the 16-bit value before storage. Otherwise try the third slot at $A1A0.

Return if $94B4 is set. Otherwise play effect $0D, call $C04C, set $94B4, call $FEA7, store the resulting direction at $94B7 and position bytes at $94AA–$94AC. Directions 5 or more subtract $10 from the 16-bit value before storage.
Increment $94B1. Value 3 wraps to zero and updates slot 0, value 1 updates slot 1, and other values update slot 2.
For motion index 1, check the map, check overlap, check indexed overlap with Y=0, then dispatch motion and return.

If $94B2 is clear select the empty-slot sprite at $A220. Otherwise copy the slot's direction and three position bytes from $94B5/$94A4-$94A6 into working state $9498-$949B, set slot selector $94B8 to zero, run $A209 and copy the changed position bytes back.

If $94B3 is clear select the empty-slot sprite at $A220. Otherwise load working direction and position from $94B6/$94A7-$94A9, set slot selector $94B8 to 1, run $A209 and save the three changed position bytes back.

If $94B4 is clear select the empty-slot sprite at $A220. Otherwise load working direction and position from $94B7/$94AA-$94AC, set slot selector $94B8 to 2, run $A209 and save the three changed position bytes back.

Scene-actor state beside the pointer sequences. The direct readers and writers in $A36A-$AFCC use these bytes for placement, contact flags, animation steps and update dividers. $A303 is the active animation phase used by the $AF15 path; the following tables begin at $A31A.
Last three bytes before the first 22-entry scene animation table. These continue the state group beginning at $A2D7.

Twenty-two pointer values selected by $AF7A for $FC29: $8A, $88, $86, $84, $86, $88 repeated three times, followed by $8A, $88, $86, $84. These select the even-numbered sprite slots $84–$8A. The table matches in the entry and play snapshots.

Twenty-two pointer values selected by $AF7A for $8018: $8B, $89, $87, $85, $87, $89 repeated three times, followed by $8B, $89, $87, $85. These select the odd-numbered sprite slots $85–$8B. The table matches in the entry and play snapshots.

Thirty stored bytes following the two 22-entry animation tables. The normal cycle feeding $AF7A supplies indices 1 through 21, so that reader stops at $A345. The bytes resemble further sprite sequences ($98-$A7 and $03); another consumer remains unresolved.
Six stored values indexed by X at $A3C8 when restoring the alternate screen detail. They follow the two main pointer tables and their retained tail.
If $A2D8 is zero, copy 512 codes from $1400 to $4400 and return. Otherwise follow the partial-copy and patch path at $A381.
Copy selected ranges from the alternate screen to $4400–$45FF, then repeat six bytes from $A364 in eight screen rows. This is the nonzero-$A2D8 branch of $A36A.
Write X to the actor sprite pointer at $FC29 and A to its paired pointer at $8018. Increment animation counter $A2E5 and return it in A.
Select sprite pointer $63 and a paired pointer cycling through $20-$27. Every fifth call through $A3E7, reset $A2E5 and advance the immediate paired-pointer operand at $A3F7, wrapping $28 to $20.
Select sprite pointer $62 and a paired pointer cycling through $40-$47. Every fifth call reset $A2E5 and advance the immediate paired-pointer operand at $A417, wrapping $48 to $40.
Select sprite pointer $67 and a paired pointer cycling through $50-$57. Every fifth call reset $A2E5 and advance the immediate paired-pointer operand at $A437, wrapping $58 to $50.
Select sprite pointer $66 and a paired pointer cycling through $30-$37. Every fifth call reset $A2E5 and advance the immediate paired-pointer operand at $A457, wrapping $38 to $30.
Mark Janosz hurt and remove two strength-gauge rows by calling $A480 twice. The full gauge has twenty rows, so ten hits empty it unless intervening updates restore rows. Verified in VICE.

Copy one empty row into Janosz's strength sprite at $6580 and advance the self-modified operands by three. At source low byte $FC, set $A2F9/$A2FE and reset the phase counter. $A585 then advances to phase 1 after the collapse animation.
Set phase-1 hurt flag $A2F3 and enter the shared opponent-strength update. The callers require both stored beam-hit flags, which may include a stale flag from a switched-off beam.
Set phase-2 hurt flag $A301 and enter the shared opponent-strength update. The callers require both stored beam-hit flags, which may include a stale flag from a switched-off beam.
Increment $A2F6. When it reaches 2, clear it and call $A4FF; otherwise return.

Remove one row from the opponent-strength sprite at $6500. This runs every second damage-entry call, so twenty rows take forty calls without restoration. Exhaustion sets $A2FA/$A300 in phase 1 or $A302 in phase 2. The collapse sequence advances to phase 2 or wins. Damage entry requires both stored hit flags; they need not represent two currently active beams.

Update the active-position actor first. A room mismatch hides its paired sprite. With phase zero, $A2F9 advances a five-by-five animation into phase 1; otherwise $A2F1 copies a reverse bitmap byte every 16 calls and walks the four source/destination operands back by three. Other phases dispatch through $A645. The shared exit hides the actor when its room differs from $8041.

In phase 0, an empty Janosz strength gauge ($A2F9) runs a five-by-five collapse animation and sets phase $8050 to 1. Otherwise restore one depleted strength row every sixteen calls while the hurt flag is set. Nonzero phases dispatch to Vigo's scene logic.

Compare actor Y at $FC19 with target Y at $A30E. Equality sets $A312. A smaller Y selects down animation and probes the floor at Y index 4 through $B84B; a larger Y selects up animation and probes through $B752. If the probe reports an open step through $A2E3, adjust actor Y by one in that direction.

Compare $804C with $A30F. If they differ, choose the $A434 path when $804C is 1 and the $A454 path otherwise. If they match, compare the stored pair $FC09/$FC11 with $A30C/$A30D: equal bytes set $A313 to 1 and return; otherwise the comparisons select one of those two paths. Each path sets $A2E4 to 1, calls a directional helper with Y initially 4, and calls $ACC5 or $ACE6 only when $A2E3 is nonzero. The $B95F entry resets Y to zero before its shared helper. The target is a surviving Ghostbuster chosen by $AABE, which saves its coordinates and room.

If $FC11 equals $A30D and $FC09 equals $A30C, set $A313 to 1 and return. If the high bytes match but the low bytes differ, choose the $A454 path when $FC09 is lower and the $A434 path otherwise. If the high bytes differ, choose the $A454 path when $FC11 is zero and the $A434 path otherwise. Each path sets $A2E4 and conditionally calls another helper when $A2E3 is nonzero.
Copy the saved three-byte scene actor position at $A2DC-$A2DE into $FC0A/$FC12/$FC1A.

When $A2DA is zero, select blank pointer 3 at $FC2A and return. Otherwise check the active position against the grid and both player positions, then dispatch state $A2E2 values 1, 2, 3 or 4 to $A833, $A7DA, $A8E5 or $A88C respectively.

Animate the enemy attack through $98-$9B while moving right four and up two pixels per call. Clear $A2DA at the room edge. Other directional entries use the corresponding $9C-$9F sequence. The common hit test $A9D5 removes ten player-strength rows.

Subtract 12 from the 16-bit position at $A2DC/$A2DD and divide its low byte by 8 for a column. Subtract $32 from $A2DE with byte wrap and divide by 8 for a row. Use that row to select a screen-row address at $8428, add the column, and add 31 if the adjusted position high byte is nonzero. Add $AC to the resulting address high byte with ADC, retaining the carry from the preceding high-byte addition; if $804E is nonzero, add 4 to that high byte with carry cleared. Patch the load at $A9B9 to this address. If the loaded byte is 1, clear $A2DA. This resembles the grid check at $9321, but that routine clears carry before adding $AC; the meaning of the active state remains open.
Call the active-position overlap check at $A9D5 with X and Y both zero, then again with X equal to 1 and Y equal to 2; return.

Test the active enemy attack against the selected same-room Ghostbuster. On overlap, apply ten player-strength depletion calls, play effect $19, and clear the attack flag $A2DA. Coordinates are halved for the horizontal comparison.

Clear target-alignment flags $A312/$A313 and advance the random byte. Prefer the first or second player's coordinates according to its low bit, but skip a player whose state is 4 when the other branch is available. Save that player's X low/high and Y at $A30C-$A30E and its room at $A30F.
Store A, X and Y as target X low, X high and Y at $A30C-$A30E, clear $A311 and return.

Check placement overlap, advance $A2E8 and increment path index $A2E7 every fourth call. At index $B0 reset the actor position and alternate the source operand between tables $B08B and $B13E, then reset the index. Read a direction byte into $A2D9 and dispatch values 1-4 with X=0 to the four actor movement routines.

Select sprite $6A when X is zero or $6E otherwise, and a paired pointer cycling through $38-$3F. Move actor Y down one and X right twice. Every fourth call through shared counter $A2E9, advance the paired-pointer operand and wrap $40 to $38.

Select sprite $68 when X is zero or $6C otherwise, and a paired pointer cycling through $28-$2F. Move actor Y up one and X right twice. Every fourth call through shared counter $A2E9, advance the paired-pointer operand and wrap $30 to $28.

Select sprite $69 when X is zero or $6D otherwise, and a paired pointer cycling through $48-$4F. Move actor Y up one and X left twice. Every fourth call through shared counter $A2E9, advance the paired-pointer operand and wrap $50 to $48.

Select sprite $6B when X is zero or $6F otherwise, and a paired pointer cycling through $58-$5F. Move actor Y down one and X left twice. Every fourth call through shared counter $A2E9, advance the paired-pointer operand and wrap $60 to $58.
Decrement actor Y at $FC19 and return.
Increment actor Y at $FC19 and return.
With high X zero and low X below 5, clear $804C, set $803D and move to X=$0160. Otherwise subtract one from the 16-bit actor X twice.
With high X nonzero and low X at least $60, set $804C and move to X=$0005. Otherwise add one to the 16-bit actor X twice.
With high X zero and low X below 5, enter the room-wrap setup at $AC88; otherwise subtract one from actor X at $ACD4.
Subtract one from the actor's two-byte X position at $FC09/$FC11.
With high X nonzero and low X at least $60, enter the room-wrap setup at $ACAE; otherwise add one to actor X at $ACF5.
Add one to the actor's two-byte X position at $FC09/$FC11.

While Oscar is dropped ($9485), compare his room and position with Janosz. An overlap resets Oscar to the crib through $AD76, clearing carried/dropped flags and restoring room 1 coordinates $00C5,$A5.
Clear $8046, $947E, $9485 and $8048; set $8047 to $C5, $8049 to $A5 and $804D to 1; then call the museum screen setup routine and return.

If $A302 is nonzero, call the phase step and return. Otherwise, if $A301 is nonzero, call the reverse paired-match copy and return. If $A303 is nonzero, set $A2E6 to 1 and call $AABE when $A2E6 was zero; otherwise continue at $ADD0. If none of those flags is set, set $C319 to 1 and return when $8026 is zero; otherwise advance the scene animation and jump to $A62E. At $ADD0, decrement $803C up to five times until it becomes zero. If it does not become zero, jump to $A65D. If it does, call $8458, copy $803B to $803C, $804C to $804E, and $FC09/$FC11/$FC19 to $A2DC/$A2DD/$A2DE; set $A2DA to 1, copy $A2D9 to $A2E2, and return. The state identities remain open.
When $A2FA is set, enter the five-by-five phase animation at $AE13. Otherwise inspect the pending reverse-copy and scene-animation flags at $AE8A.

Advance the five-by-five collapse animation. After 25 calls, phase 1 resets Vigo's twenty-row gauge and enters phase 2; phase 2 jumps to congratulations at $0A16. These transitions were verified in VICE and the CPU model.

While the relevant hurt flag is set, restore one Vigo strength row every eight calls, reversing $A4FF's self-modified pointers. Stop restoration at the full-gauge source and clear the corresponding phase flag.

Increment $A2FB and return unless it reaches 5. Then clear it and increment $A2FC. Values below $16 enter $AF7A to select paired sprite pointers. At $16, clear $A2FC; if $8050 is 2, set $A303, select pointer $60 and write 5 to $FC21. Otherwise set $A2FD and $A2D8, call the screen setup, select pointer $6F and write 8 to $FC21. Both paths set $8018 to $58, $FC09/$FC11 to $E8/$00, $FC19 to $71 and $804C to 1. The animated object and transition remain to be identified. This selects the opponent's collapse/emergence animation. In phase 1 it prepares the moving Vigo actor; phase 2 prepares the final actor using the first Ghostbuster's green colour and normal facing sprite.

Use Y as an index into the tables at $A31A and $A330, writing the selected pointers to $FC29 and $8018. If voice 3 has no active effect, start effect $14. Then set $FC09/$FC11 to $FF/$00, $FC19 to $50, $FC21 to $0A and $804C to 1. The path at $AF15 supplies indices 1–21 during its normal counter cycle.

Call $AFF5, then decrement $803C up to four times and return unless it reaches zero. When it does, return if $A2DA is nonzero; otherwise call $8458, copy $803B to $803C and $804C to $804E, copy $FC09/$FC11/$FC19 to $A2DC/$A2DD/$A2DE, start sound effect $13, set $A2DA to 1 and copy $A2D9 to $A2E2. The gameplay identity remains open.

Advance $A2ED and increment path index $A2EC every fourth call. At index $B1, reset actor X/Y and sprites, set its room, alternate the path source between $B1F2 and $B2A4, and reset the index. Read a direction byte into $A2D9 and dispatch values 1-4 with X=1 to the four actor movement routines.

First direction table selected by the self-modified read at $AB5E. The normal updater uses its first 176 bytes, four calls per index: 1 moves down-right, 2 up-right, 3 up-left and 4 down-left. The stored $04,$00,$00 at the end lie beyond that cycle's read bound.

Alternate direction table selected by $AB5E when the first actor's path toggles. The normal updater reads indices 0-$AF with the same four diagonal-direction codes as $B08B. Four stored bytes $04,$04,$00,$00 follow the normal read bound.

First direction table selected by the self-modified read at $B05D. Its normal cycle reads 177 bytes, indices 0-$B0, with four calls per index. Codes 1-4 select down-right, up-right, up-left and down-left movement. The following stored zero is outside that read bound.
Alternate 177-byte direction table selected by $B05D after the second actor's path toggles. Indices 0-$B0 select the same four diagonal movement routines, called with X=1.
Five input and transition state bytes preceding the result-entry stubs at $B35A. The keyboard and selected-player paths read and update these values before movement dispatch.
Pass X=2 and Y=1 to the shared story-restoration routine. Adjacent entries pass Y=2 and Y=0 with the same episode index.

Scan keyboard matrix rows, including Space. When $8028 is zero, a new Space press toggles $8042 between 0 and 1, calls $86B6 with the selected entry from $8026/$8027 and may call $8396. It then selects the corresponding offsets in $B356 and $B357 and continues to joystick movement at $B459. The earlier key scans can divert or wait before reaching that point.

Read joystick port 2 into $803F and select directional movement. Up takes precedence over down; within either vertical path left takes precedence over right. With neither vertical direction, left takes precedence over right. The selected path writes values to $FC25/$FC26 indexed by $B356, calls movement helpers and advances a four-update animation counter at $8040; the animation's next value is kept in the immediate operand of the path's load instruction.

Add $B358 to the selected low X byte at $FC05,Y and propagate the carry into $FC0D,Y, saving the result at $805F/$8061. Add $B359 to the selected Y byte at $FC15,Y and save it at $8060. Subtract $24 from the two-byte X result and $32 from the Y byte; shift their low bytes right three places into $8062/$8063. Movement helpers call this to prepare cell coordinates.

Copy $FC05 and $FC07 into $8052/$8053, then shift the low bit of $FC0D/$FC0F into the high bit of those bytes. This produces the low eight bits of each position divided by two. Advance the descent, then read joystick port 2. Up decreases $8058 unless it is zero; otherwise down increases it while it is below 7. If both are held, the up path takes precedence.

Restore one saved screen/colour cell of the nineteen-cell descent rope in reverse order. At zero remaining cells, enter the outcome handler. A fast fatal landing animates before reaching this path.
